title: Ranger X
subtitle: A machine and its support vehicle
summary: Ranger X is GAU Entertainment's action shooter, first released for Mega Drive in Japan on 28 May 1993.
body: Ranger X is GAU Entertainment's action shooter, first released for Mega Drive in Japan on 28 May 1993. The player pilots a heavily armed flying machine through missions presented with side-scrolling action and introductory wireframe views. Each stage sets targets to destroy before the final confrontation can begin. A support motorcycle called Indra accompanies the main machine, giving the battlefield another moving component. The combination makes positioning unusually important: the player is managing a flying weapon and a ground vehicle within the same stretch of terrain.

The jetpack lifts Ranger X into the air, but its rising temperature limits sustained flight. Landing gives it time to cool, turning the ground into a necessary part of movement rather than something to avoid. The pulse rifle provides a dependable attack, while special weapons draw on a separate energy reserve. Their different uses invite the player to choose equipment for the targets ahead. Flight, landing and firing form a cycle in which a useful elevated position must be balanced against the need to recover and move again.

Bright areas replenish the energy used by special weapons, making illumination part of the stage's practical geography. Indra can move and fire independently, and entering it provides another protective shield. Those systems create several reasons to change position during a mission: a target may require a better angle, a flight may need to cool down, or a weapon may need more energy. The layered backgrounds and mechanical animation make those spaces impressive to watch, but their strongest contribution is giving the player's machinery several interacting ways to survive inside them.
